title: Stable positive delay mixtures miss two-window AOU ranges in one eastern North Pacific tile
abstract: We test whether extra transport delays can explain the spatial errors of a published North Pacific ventilation model on density 26.5. We form convex hulls of two-window AOU changes over 20 runs, all retained cells and added delays of 0-20 years. Fourteen of fifteen observed tile uncertainty rectangles intersect the stable-mixture hull. The 35-40 N, 130-120 W tile does not: its large 2009-2015 gain and smaller 2016-2025 gain cannot both be matched. A sharp linear program requires at least 22.4 percent changed mixture weight between windows, or 9.8 percent with wider oxygen-use rates. Four-year delays need no pre-1980 extension and retain the conflict. Different sampling support can remove it. The test therefore constrains stationary added-delay explanations but does not establish a second ocean process. Code, licensed aggregate inputs, separation proof, sensitivity tests and figures are supplied.

display.caption: Stable delay mixtures and observed two-window AOU changes in an eastern and a western North Pacific tile.

citations.reason: Verified published model maps and tile aggregates; tests its proposed slower-transport explanation.
